11.text: Of the same type were two brothers, Čêpaˊt and Qančiuˊ, from the so-

12.text: called Kavraˊlɪn traders.¹ It has been related before that the Kavraˊlɪn traders

13.text: are of Maritime origin, but have reindeer of their own, and travel all their

14.text: lives between the Maritime villages and the Reindeer camps, carrying seal-

15.text: skins and thongs, beaver-skins and marten-skins, and also American rifles,

16.text: knives, etc., and exchanging them for fawn-skins and ready-made clothes of

17.text: reindeer-skin, also for Russian brick-tea and leaf-tobacco. I have met the two

18.text: brothers several times at the yearly Anui fair. Both were men of tall stature

19.text: and of considerable physical strength. Čêpaˊt was said to have killed several

20.text: men. Qančiuˊ, on the other hand, had lost one eye in a scuffle, and bore

21.text: deep scars on his breast, the results of old knife-wounds. The brothers were

22.text: widely known among the Reindeer camps of the Anui country, also among

23.text: the Russian traders and Cossacks. They came usually with abundant means

24.text: for purchases, but a good part of their property was spent in buying brandy.

25.text: They themselves drank and treated others to drink. Čêpaˊt was the cause

26.text: of the brawl mentioned before,² which took place in 1895.

27.text: The chief officer of the Kolyma did not go that spring to the Anui fair.

28.text: Instead, his assistant went, a man quite new to the country, who did not know

29.text: the methods of Chukchee trading. He brought with him some Cossacks from

30.text: Sredne-Kolymsk, who were but little acquainted with the Chukchee, and gave

31.text: them strict orders, first of all, to stop the sale of strong liquors. This would

32.text: have been quite praiseworthy; but, at the same time, almost all traders, men

33.text: and even women, and among others the commanders of the Cossacks,³ brought

34.text: a quantity of liquor for sale to the natives. It was labelled as “destined

35.text: for private use.” The assistant officer then ordered the Cossacks to take
